correctness.rationale: For the four-simplex on five vertices, 31 nonempty faces, an optimal Morse matching uses 15 incidence pairs and leaves exactly one critical vertex (Euler/Morse constraints). Rooting that vertex at zero converts the full S5 orbit question to S4 orbits of perfect Hasse matchings of the remaining 30 faces. The least-unmatched-mask recurrence lists each perfect matching once and no others, giving exactly 117837 candidates; orient every Hasse cover upward except matched edges reversed, test the resulting full directed graph for acyclicity (equivalently no closed Forman V-path). An independent C++ enumeration and the pinned distinct Python method confirm 76025 acyclic rooted matchings and S4 fixed counts 76025, 243, 21, 8, 1 for cycle types 1^4, 2.1^2, 2^2, 3.1, 4. Burnside numerator 76025+6*243+3*21+8*8+6*1=77616 yields exactly 3234 orbits. Matching stabilizer counts 74568 trivial,1368 transposition,60 double transposition,28 S3,1 S4 sum to 76025 and give 3107+114+5+7+1=3234 orbits. The explicit S4-fixed cone pairing verifies the final singleton. This is an exhaustive finite certificate for the whole finite five-vertex simplex, not partial sampling.
residual_risks: The finite result does not determine the homotopy type of the entire Morse complex or higher-dimensional simplex symmetry profiles.
